title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system and set the Euler angles to -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees. Ensure the translation vector is set to (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. Within this face, draw a single loop and within this loop, draw a circle centered at (0.0476, 0.0476) with a radius of 0.0476. Apply a scaling factor of 0.0952 to the entire sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles and translating it using the translation vector specified in the coordinate system. Extrude the transformed sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Finally, create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The resulting cylindrical object will have a length of 0.09525 units, a width of 0.09525 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the sketch
circle_center = (0.0476, 0.0476)
circle_radius = 0.0476

# Create the sketch on the XY plane
r = r.center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.extrude(extrude_depth).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the base of the cylinder
r = r.center(0.0476, 0.0476).circle(0.0476)

# Extrude the circle to create the cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
